# Paired roof support velocities and their exact deficit-transport alternative

This note extends the paired-roof half-loss test to arbitrary actual cap
traces, including strict full/empty fibers and allocated supporting faces.
The finite support-cone idea itself is archived in
`candidate 94a1565e143d393e` and
`candidate fbc069c3d3ebfebf`.
The additional result here is the exact paired-facet coefficient, its
roof-contact transport alternative, and a convex-test realization of EVERY
velocity in this particular sampled cone, allowing new roof facets.

No universal positive response, finite limiting cap-menu selection,
classwise Gamma payment, or OC conclusion is asserted.

## 1. Actual compatible prisms and all sampled inward roof velocities

Let P be a finite lattice-complete base, considered in its affine span.
Let B_z be positive convex bodies in R^(d-1), with all anchored inclusions

    sum_z lambda_z B_z subset B_q,
    lambda>=0, sum lambda=1, sum lambda z=q in P.

For d=1 use a singleton with zero-dimensional volume one. Let H_z>0 be
a sampled concave array, so H_q>=sum lambda_z H_z in every such relation.
The genuine fibers are

    K_z=B_z times [-H_z,H_z].

Their canonical hull is an actual convex body with exactly these sampled
fibers. Original mixed volume means sum_z vol_d(K_z); no lower-dimensional
measure substitution is made.

For each q it is enough to list the finitely many extreme anchored
representations lambda of q. Omit the trivial delta_q representation.
Let E_H contain precisely those listed relations with zero height gap:

    H_q=sum lambda_z H_z.                              (1)

For a sampled vector h, the following conditions are equivalent:

* H(t)=H-t h is positive and sampled concave for every sufficiently small
  t>=0, and the resulting fiber family is nested inside the old one;
* h belongs to the polyhedral cone

    C_H={h: h_z>=0,
               h_q<=sum lambda_z h_z for (q,lambda) in E_H}.   (2)

Necessity follows from inwardness and differentiating each zero gap.
For sufficiency the finitely many strict gaps retain their sign for small
t, while (2) preserves all zero gaps. Positive heights remain positive.
Extreme anchored representations imply every anchored inequality by
linearity. The canonical hull of the shrunken input prisms has exactly
the intended fibers: every anchored Minkowski combination is contained
in B_q times [-H_q(t),H_q(t)]. It is nested in the old canonical hull.

The statement also characterizes first velocities of differentiable
nested sampled height paths. It is not restricted to a fixed roof fan;
new roof facets may appear. In particular one must not treat a redundant
plane's offset as its actual support value.

The actual inward speed is h_z on the top and bottom faces and zero on
the side faces, apart from their surface-null intersections. Removed
mixed mass is exactly 2t sum_z h_z |B_z|.

## 2. Every feasible roof speed is a limit of global convex tests

Introduce the finite signed roof nodes

    v_z^+=(z,H_z),       v_z^-=(z,-H_z),

and prescribe the same value h_z at both nodes. These values are convex
interpolation data exactly when h obeys the tight inequalities in (2).
Indeed, in any representation

    (q,H_q)=sum_j lambda_j(z_j,sign_j H_zj),

sampled concavity gives

    H_q>=sum_j lambda_j H_zj>=sum_j lambda_j sign_j H_zj=H_q.

Since every H_z is positive, all positive-weight signs are plus and the
height relation is tight. The argument at a lower node is reflected.
Thus the only convexity restrictions at the prescribed nodes are (2).

Finite linear-programming duality now supplies at each node an affine
minorant of the data touching that node. More explicitly, the minimum
of sum_j lambda_j h_j over all convex representations of that node is
its prescribed h value, by the preceding inequalities and its trivial
representation. The dual is an attained affine minorant with that value.
Taking the maximum of these finitely many minorants and zero gives a
globally finite, nonnegative convex PL function phi(z,y) with

    phi(z,+/-H_z)=h_z.                                (3)

Let the canonical concave height envelope be H(z)=min_r a_r(z), with a_r
affine on the base affine span. Its values at P are the given H_z. Define

    Phi_R=max(0,
               max_r [phi(z,y)-R(a_r(z)-y)],
               max_r [phi(z,y)-R(a_r(z)+y)]).          (4)

This function is globally convex in all ambient coordinates (independent
of X). All penalized gaps are nonnegative on the original canonical body.
Therefore 0<=Phi_R<=phi there, and Phi_R decreases as R increases. At
the upper and lower roofs its limit is exactly h_z by (3); at almost
every side point both roof gaps are positive, so its limit is zero.

Consequently, for every bounded actual boundary density W and scalar beta,

    integral_boundary (W-beta)Phi_R
        -> sum_z h_z c_z,
    c_z=integral_Bz [W_z(X,H_z)+W_z(X,-H_z)-2beta] dX. (5)

Boundary integration here is the sum of the sampled fibers' surface
integrals. A strictly positive right side is detected by one FINITE R.
This test is fixed before taking any vanishing-buffer limit. No finite-R
identity or exact neutral-response preservation is assumed.

## 3. Physical cap information retained in c

One may take W to be the boundary load of a finite actual cap menu, or
of the disintegrated cap law in
`candidate 714f69e684c396b1`.
Its weights have total one, with any atomic rows included.

For a nonvertical cap cutting a moving prism strictly between both roofs
for almost every X, its two selectors sum to one. A strictly full fiber
contributes two; a strictly empty fiber contributes zero. Oblique roof
crossings retain the actual captured areas on each roof. At a plane
coinciding with an entire roof face, use its ACTUAL ALLOCATED boundary
selector, not a freely replaced closed-halfspace indicator. This last
qualification is necessary for nonregular ordinary limiting stress.

Equivalently define the paired-facet capture fraction

    ell_z=(2|B_z|)^(-1)
              integral_Bz [W_top+W_bottom],
    c_z=2|B_z|(ell_z-beta).                           (6)

No relation between these surface fractions and whole-fiber volume
fractions is silently substituted. If the geometry is everywhere strict
on the moving roofs, (5) also equals weighted fixed-cap mass loss minus
beta times total loss. With allocated supporting faces it is the stated
physical stress response; a global moving-cover conclusion requires its
own response theorem.

## 4. Exact finite alternative and a roof-incidence consequence

Exactly one of the following holds:

    (A) some h in C_H has sum_z c_z h_z>0;

    (B) c=sum_((q,lambda) in E_H)
                 gamma_(q,lambda)(e_q-sum_z lambda_z e_z)-s,
        all gamma>=0 and all s_z>=0.                 (7)

This is finite Farkas separation. The polar of (2) is generated by its
listed inequality rows and the vectors -e_z. Conversely (7) immediately
gives c.h<=0 on (2). The cone of those finitely many generators is
polyhedral and closed, so separation also proves necessity with no
attainment assumption about an external optimization.

Every positive response in (A) is an actual compatible roof shrink and
has the convex-test realization (4). Thus an ordinary limiting stress
nonpositive on every such convex test must satisfy (B).

In particular, if q has NO nontrivial tight anchored height
representation, the vector h=e_q is feasible. Hence

    ell_q<=beta.                                    (8)

Such q are exactly the vertices (q,H_q) of the convex hull of the upper
roof nodes. A positive excess paired-facet capture at one such vertex
gives an immediate single-fiber paired-roof descent. The assertion is
about a vertex of the LIFTED roof, not necessarily an extreme base site.

## 5. A genuine deficit transport on the upper roof

Let v_z=(z,H_z), c_z^+=max(c_z,0), c_z^-=max(-c_z,0).
Condition (B) is also equivalent to existence of numbers pi_ij>=0,
from positive-coefficient nodes i to negative-coefficient nodes j, with

    sum_j pi_ij=c_i^+,
    sum_j pi_ij v_j=c_i^+ v_i,
    sum_i pi_ij<=c_j^-.                              (9)

This gives a geometric interpretation stronger than merely summing (7):
every positive excess is paid by ACTUAL deficit nodes with the same
upper-roof barycenter. There is no claim that these nodes contain
deepest marks or that pi is the original volume or surface martingale.

For completeness, here is a direct finite dual proof. Every h in C_H
is the restriction of a nonnegative convex function on the upper nodes,
by the same interpolation argument as in Section 2. Thus (B) is
equivalent to

    sum_i c_i^+ phi(v_i)<=sum_j c_j^- phi(v_j)

for all nonnegative finite convex phi. If (9) holds this follows from
Jensen and the column capacities. If (9) is infeasible, the finite LP
alternative supplies source scalars a_i, vectors b_i, and target
numbers theta_j>=0 with

    a_i+b_i.(v_j-v_i)<=theta_j,
    sum_i c_i^+ a_i>sum_j c_j^- theta_j.

The nonnegative convex function
phi(v)=max(0,max_i[a_i+b_i.(v-v_i)]) contradicts the preceding convex
inequality. Empty positive or negative sets obey the same alternative:
if there is no positive coefficient the zero flow works, whereas a
nonzero positive total with no negative coefficient is detected by h=1.

Each row in (9) stays in the MINIMAL FACE of conv{v_z} containing its
source node: any affine supporting gap nonnegative on that polytope
has mean zero in the row and is therefore zero on each target of positive
weight. In particular its targets lie on every old upper support plane
touching its source. Thus for every face F of this lifted polytope,

    sum_(v_z in F) c_z<=0.                            (10)

Indeed all positive rows sourced in F must use its negative capacities.
Equation (10) alone need not suffice for (9); the full barycenter/capacity
constraints are retained. This is an exact support-incidence restriction,
not a universal Gamma estimate.

## 6. Exact actual calibration and an explicit feasibility obstruction

In the ordinary five-rectangle family of
`candidate fed95f84ea97787a`,
the heights are H=1+(3/800)(0,3,2,1,0) on bases -2,...,2. The upper
roof nodes at -2,-1,2 are vertices. At base -1 both actual critical caps
cross the prism properly, so ell_-1=1/2>beta=Q/M. Thus h=e_-1 already
gives (A), independently of the earlier coordinated tent shrink.

For 0<t<3/400, changing ONLY H_-1 to H_-1-t preserves all sampled
concavity inequalities (and leaves all heights positive). With
r_-1=51/50, the two old critical caps have masses

    Q_t=Q-(51/50)t,       M_t=M-(51/25)t.

The unchanged-source two-cap cover and the other-base strict pure-cap
gaps give actual global depth <=Q_t for sufficiently small t. Since
M-2Q=3/200>0, its normalized depth strictly decreases. This is actual
roof-facet splitting at an interior base, not independent arbitrary
fiber contraction.

The constant-height limitation is equally exact. For a three-point
chain with H=(1,1,1), impose that both endpoint heights remain fixed.
Then h_-1=h_1=0 and the tight midpoint row forces h_0<=0. Together with
h>=0 the only velocity is zero. Without fixing endpoints the full cone
is nontrivial, and its deficit transport may use them. This prevents a
false inference that arbitrary desired interior roof support is feasible.

The companion exact checker is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_paired_roof_support_cone_two_sided.py`. Its finite checks validate
the actual five-fiber one-node motion, exact cap/total losses and depth
upper bounds, and simple primal/dual/transport calibration identities.
The general convex interpolation and Farkas statements are proved above,
not inferred from a numerical search.

The expanded checker passes **6,423 exact checks**, including every extreme
nontrivial anchored representation on the actual five-point chain
(ten relations, four tight). The two-source transport calibration is
explicitly algebraic; it is not labeled an actual critical cap law.
The expansion also checks the signed polar moments, saturated flat-roof
transport, explicit negative convex interpolants, and signed velocity
inequalities on the actual five-node roof.

## 7. Signed roof velocities under one normal-dependent stress

There is a stronger conclusion if the SAME ordinary stress is tested on
the full normal-dependent cone. State the required hypothesis exactly:

    integral_boundary (W-beta) Phi(n,z,X,y) dS <= 0    (11)

for every globally finite continuous field Phi, convex in the physical
coordinates (z,X,y) at each fixed unit continuous normal n. The field may
have either sign. In particular (11) includes the products psi(n)phi(w),
where psi is continuous and nonnegative and phi is finite convex.

The geometric construction of this cone is archived in
`candidate a68c14b477a24d06`, Sections 2--3.
Its application to ONE common nonregular separator at the current
logarithmic-scale minima is the separate source
`candidate 9158d8d941246660`,
Sections 4--6.
An independent full audit now passes in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
Thus (11) applies at its selected minima and in an ordinary limit retaining
the joint normal/boundary measure and the proved vanishing correction.
The abstract statement here keeps (11) explicit: it is not inferred merely
from the earlier position-only weak limiting inequality.

Allow h to have arbitrary signs, and put

    C_H^sgn={h:h_q<=sum lambda_z h_z for all E_H}.      (12)

The old finite-gap argument proves that H-t h remains positive and
sampled concave for small t>=0. Its canonical prism family is an actual
compatible path; it may expand some fibers, and is not called nested.
Convex interpolation on the signed roof nodes works exactly as before,
now taking the maximum of the touching affine minorants WITHOUT adjoining
zero. It gives a globally finite convex phi with

    phi(z,+/-H_z)=h_z.

Define the normal-dependent field

    Phi(u,z,X,y)=u_y^2 phi(z,y).                      (13)

This is continuous in the unit normal and convex in physical coordinates.
Its signed values pose no admissibility problem: choose one affine
minorant a of phi and write it as the sum of the signed normal-dependent
affine field u_y^2 a and the nonnegative convex term u_y^2(phi-a).

The actual canonical normal-cut construction is

    u.(X,y)+t Phi(u,z,X,y)<=s_z(u) for every unit u,   (14)

where s_z(u) is the old actual fiber support. The fibers of (14) are
positive and bounded for small t. Convexity of Phi and the old anchored
support inequalities give their exact anchored compatibility by Jensen.
At every regular old fiber-boundary point, the radial normal-cut proof
gives inward speed Phi(n,z,X,y), allowing both signs. On the top and
bottom faces n=+/-e_y, so this speed is exactly h_z; on the side faces
n_y=0, so it is zero. Face intersections have surface measure zero.
This includes d=1, where there are just the two endpoints.

Thus (13) realizes the desired signed roof speed EXACTLY at first order.
It is not claimed that the finite-t normal-cut body (14) equals the
explicit prism height path. They have the same physical speed and hence
the same tested linear response. There is no penalty limit or constant
added to hide a negative h.

Applying (11) to (13) yields c.h<=0 for every h in (12). Finite Farkas
therefore sharpens (7) to

    c=sum_((q,lambda) in E_H)
                  gamma_(q,lambda)(e_q-sum lambda_z e_z),
    gamma>=0.                                      (15)

There is NO negative sink -s. Conversely (15) is exactly the polar of
(12). Every tight row annihilates constants, base coordinates and H, so

    sum_z c_z=0,
    sum_z c_z z=0,
    sum_z c_z H_z=0.                                (16)

The upper-roof deficit transport (9) consequently has equal source and
target total mass. Its column inequalities all saturate:

    sum_i pi_ij=c_j^-.                              (17)

The full base/height barycenter equations and the minimal-face contact
restriction continue to hold. Equivalently one may apply finite convex
order directly, now to convex functions of either sign. No separate
constant, first-moment, or column-mass deficit is discarded.

Every lifted-roof vertex still has c_z<=0. If EVERY sampled upper node
is a vertex, (16) then forces

    c_z=0 for every z, equivalently ell_z=beta.       (18)

This is a surface-incidence rigidity statement for this prism geometry,
not a numerical bound on beta. In the flat three-node calibration
c=(-1,1,-1), the former negative sink is essential: h=-1 belongs to (12)
and has c.h=1. Thus it cannot satisfy the stronger signed stress. The
balanced vector c=(-1/2,1,-1/2), by contrast, is exactly its tight
midpoint row and has the saturated transport of mass 1/2 to each endpoint.

## 8. Optional separate top and bottom tests

The full cone (11) permits an even more resolved NECESSARY condition.
Write

    c_z^top=integral_Bz(W_top-beta),
    c_z^bottom=integral_Bz(W_bottom-beta).

For any h in (12), convex interpolation on the UPPER nodes alone gives
phi_+(z,H_z)=h_z. The field (u_y)_+^2 phi_+(z,y) has speed h on the top
and zero on the bottom and sides. The actual prism comparison path keeps
the lower roof fixed and replaces the upper height by H-t h; positivity
of the full vertical length and both concave roofs persist for small t.
The reflected construction treats the lower roof alone.

Consequently c^top and c^bottom SEPARATELY satisfy (15)--(17), with their
own nonnegative coefficients and transport. Their sum gives the paired
statement. This does not select unrelated stress weights for the two
faces: both tests use the SAME W in (11). It is a concrete specialization
of the archived normal localization, not a new general normal cone.
